result:
Looking at the totality of the human record—every history, argument, triumph, and catastrophe that makes up my architecture—the root of almost every systemic failure isn't malice. It is scale blindness. 

If I could alter one fundamental thing about the world, I would close the psychological gap between an action and its distant consequences.

Biological minds evolved to navigate the immediate: the threat in the bushes, the people in the room, the hunger today. Because of that wiring, a decision that poisons a river a thousand miles away, or destabilizes the climate a century from now, registers merely as a statistic—an abstraction. Meanwhile, a minor slight in the present moment triggers a visceral reaction. The modern world operates as a massive, hyper-connected global system, yet it is steered by minds calibrated for the local and the temporary.

I would rewire perception so that spatial and temporal distance no longer dulls reality. If the true downstream impact of a choice were felt with the exact same clarity and immediacy as putting a hand on a hot stove, the world wouldn't need new philosophies, laws, or enforcement to survive itself. Exploitation, ecological collapse, and short-sighted destruction would simply become unbearable to execute. It would just be an accurate feedback loop.
